lines: A camera on your head. Handled honestly.

claims_allowlist: IronPal is a headband that watches your set from your point of view and logs the exercise, your reps and the weight.
You type nothing; the log fills itself in.
The old way is thumb-typing sets into a phone between sets, and the numbers get fudged or skipped.
Reps and exercise recognition run on the band itself, offline, and never leave it.
Reading the weight sends a single frame off-device; it is processed in seconds and deleted immediately.
IronPal does not store your footage.
The band has an 8 mm flush camera lens, a single teal LED and no screen.
It is a first-person view: it sees what you see.
Reading arbitrary free weights from a first-person camera is the hard problem being built, not a finished or guaranteed feature.
After a set the app proposes the exercise, reps and weight, and one tap confirms it.
Each exercise accumulates clean sets and earns a level: Recon, then Provisional, then Certified.
IronPal is pre-launch; reserving early-bird access costs nothing today and locks the price and a 48-hour head start.
Early-bird is up to about 50% off the launch price, limited to the first 200 spots.
IronPal is built in the open by a solo founder.
ironpal.co is where you reserve a spot.
The global health and fitness club market is about 140 billion dollars a year.
The fitness tracker market is about 50 billion dollars a year, separate from the club market.
